items.t: China Securities Regulatory Commission Chairman Wu Qing Sets "15th Five-Year Plan" Regulatory Direction: Rules on Quant Trading and Shareholding Reductions to Face Optimization Review
sum: Wu Qing, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), said at the opening ceremony of the inaugural Chinese Capital Market Academic Annual Conference in Shanghai on November 14 that the CSRC will conduct in-depth research and evaluation on the optimization of institutional rules governing quantitative trading and shareholding reductions, as well as fair and reasonable regulatory arrangements, to effectively protect investors' legitimate rights and interests. This was his first systematic articulation of the research framework for capital market regulation and reform during the "15th Five-Year Plan" period, in which market microstructure governance was listed as a separate key topic.

In his address, Wu said China's "15th Five-Year Plan" outline and the financial powerhouse "15th Five-Year Plan" have made strategic deployments for the capital market, and the CSRC has also defined development goals and key measures for the capital market during the period. Centering on major theoretical and practical issues under the new circumstances, he proposed six directions requiring deeper research, covering market characteristics and patterns, long-term stability mechanisms, institutional inclusiveness and adaptability, the two-way empowerment of artificial intelligence and the capital market, market microstructure, and participation in global financial governance.

On market microstructure, Wu proposed three specific research tasks: improving the capital supply structure and accelerating the development and expansion of long-term capital and patient capital; improving expectation-guidance mechanisms to reduce market volatility caused by "herd effects" and "short-term" trading; and evaluating the optimization of institutional rules on quantitative trading and shareholding reductions, as well as fair and reasonable regulatory arrangements.

"China's A-share market has more than 200 million stock investors and more than 800 million fund holders — a national and market condition that is unique in the world," Wu said. He said market development should draw on the general laws of mature markets while studying China's market characteristics and structural issues, and properly balance stability and progress, efficiency and fairness, and development and security.

China's Second Round of Major State Bank Capital Raises Clears Key Hurdle: ICBC, Agricultural Bank CNY 260 Billion Private Placements Approved by Shanghai Stock Exchange
sum: A new round of capital replenishment for China's large state-owned commercial banks has made key progress. On the evening of November 11, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (601398.SS) and Agricultural Bank of China (601288.SS) separately announced that their applications to issue A-shares to specific targets had both passed review by the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

According to the announcements, the two banks received the Shanghai Stock Exchange's "Exchange Review Opinion on the Issuance of Shares to Specific Targets" that day. The exchange determined that their applications to issue shares to specific targets met issuance conditions, listing conditions and information disclosure requirements. However, the placement plans have not yet completed the full regulatory process. Both ICBC and Agricultural Bank said the matter still requires a decision from the China Securities Regulatory Commission agreeing to registration before implementation, and whether registration will ultimately be granted and the specific timing remain uncertain. They will continue to fulfill information disclosure obligations in accordance with regulations.

On September 6 this year, the two banks separately disclosed their placement plans. ICBC intends to raise no more than CNY 100 billion (approximately $15.0 billion) and Agricultural Bank no more than CNY 160 billion (approximately $24.0 billion), for a combined maximum of CNY 260 billion (approximately $39.1 billion), all to be used to replenish core Tier 1 capital after deducting issuance expenses. This is the second round of capital increases by major state-owned banks, following the capital replenishment completed in 2025 by Bank of China, China Construction Bank, Bank of Communications and Postal Savings Bank of China.

In 2025, the Ministry of Finance and other entities injected funds into four major state-owned banks through private placements totaling CNY 520 billion (approximately $78.1 billion) to replenish core Tier 1 capital. The specific arrangements were as follows:

China's ICBC Loses A-Share Market Cap Crown as China Construction Bank Climbs 28% This Year to Take Top Spot
sum: China's Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (601398.SH), long the leader by market capitalization in China's A-share market, is facing sustained pressure from China Construction Bank (601939.SH) and Agricultural Bank of China (601288.SH). As of November 5, 2026, China Construction Bank's shares have gained about 28% this year, bringing its total market capitalization to CNY 3.05 trillion (approximately $457.5 billion), surpassing ICBC's CNY 2.98 trillion (approximately $447 billion); Agricultural Bank of China's total market capitalization stood at CNY 2.54 trillion (approximately $381 billion) over the same period. This marks the second change at the top of China's A-share market cap rankings, following Agricultural Bank of China's brief ascent in September 2025.

The frequent reshuffling at the top began in 2025. In September of that year, Agricultural Bank of China, riding strong share price performance, briefly overtook ICBC in total market capitalization to claim the top spot in China's A-share market for the first time. Entering 2026, Agricultural Bank of China, which had posted larger gains earlier, pulled back, and China Construction Bank took up the rally, completing its overtake of ICBC in May. During the tech stock pullback in the third quarter of 2026, ICBC briefly returned to first place, but as earnings were disclosed, China Construction Bank overtook it once again.

On valuation metrics, ICBC's current price-to-book (PB) ratio is 0.75 times, below Agricultural Bank of China's 0.89 times and China Construction Bank's 0.83 times, reflecting the market's relatively conservative pricing of its per-unit asset profitability.

On fundamentals, ICBC's scale advantage remains, but the gap is narrowing. As of the end of the third quarter of 2026, ICBC's total assets stood at CNY 57.82 trillion (approximately $8.67 trillion), continuing to rank first among China's state-owned major banks; Agricultural Bank of China's total assets were CNY 52.12 trillion (approximately $7.82 trillion), equivalent to 90% of ICBC's; China Construction Bank's total assets were CNY 48.73 trillion (approximately $7.31 trillion), about 84% of ICBC's.

sum: Technical analysis of GSK stock on November 6, 2026: price 1,890.00 GBp, trend uptrend, RSI 55.5, support 1,753.00, resistance 1,923.50.

GSK plc closed Friday's session on the London Stock Exchange (November 6, 2026) at 1,890.00 pence, unchanged from the previous close. A flat day hides the real story. The shares are up 1.89% over five days and 8.00% over one month, and a closely watched trend signal has just appeared on the chart.

That signal is a golden cross, formed two sessions before the latest session. The 20-day moving average, which tracks the recent average price, crossed above the 50-day average. Traders read it as short-term buying outpacing the longer-term trend.

Price sits above both averages: the 20-day average at 1,856.58 and the 50-day at 1,842.40. The gap between the two is only about 14 pence, so the cross is real but young. It marks a change in direction rather than a proven, established trend. The 20-day average rose 1.42% over five days, a gentle slope that points to steady drift rather than a spike.

The stock trades at 80% of its 20-day range, between support at 1,753.00 and resistance at 1,923.50. It remains well below its three-month high of 2,158.00 and comfortably above the three-month low of 1,735.50. In plain terms, the recovery has room to run before it meets the bigger ceiling, but the nearest barrier is only 33.50 pence away.
As shown in the chart, price has pulled back toward the 20-day line and held above it. This is often how healthy trends behave: a dip to the average, then a push higher.

Momentum supports the trend without being stretched. The 14-day RSI is 55.5, in neutral territory. That means buyers have the upper hand but the stock is not overbought, so the rally is not yet running on fumes. The Stochastic oscillator reads 74.7 on both %K and %D. It is also neutral, though closer to its upper zone, which hints that near-term gains could slow if the stock reaches resistance.

sum: Australian shares are set for a modest rise at Monday's open after Wall Street steadied on a rebound in AI stocks. Futures point to a 0.2 per cent gain, while the S&P 500 recovered part of its worst weekly loss since April 2025.

The Australian sharemarket is set for a positive start to the week on Monday, November 9, 2026, as Wall Street steadied after AI stocks bounced back from a two-day sell-off. Futures point to a rise of 22 points, or 0.2 per cent, at the open.
The Australian dollar was trading lower at US68.68¢ at 5.15am AEDT.

The S&P 500 rose 0.3 per cent in the latest US session. That trimmed its loss for the week to 2.7 per cent, still its worst since President Donald Trump shook markets in April 2025 with his "Liberation Day" tariffs.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 237 points, or 0.5 per cent. The Nasdaq composite climbed 1.1 per cent.

Nvidia gave the S&P 500 its biggest lift, rising 2.8 per cent after drops of 9.3 per cent and 3.2 per cent. Voters across parties say they are wary of AI and dislike higher power bills caused by data centres.

Borrowing costs add to the pressure. Worries that building more AI data centres may slow because money has become expensive to borrow were already rattling the industry. Critics had also said AI share prices were in a bubble.

[Perspective] Is the AI tide turning, starting with the stock market
sum: China’s A-shares have fallen again. But this time, they are not alone.

Asian stock markets took a collective plunge on the final trading day of the week. Yet compared with the 6% plunge in Japanese and South Korean stocks on Friday (6 November), China’s benchmark CSI 300 Index fared relatively well, closing down 1.44%.

The market turbulence was triggered by a sell-off in Wall Street technology stocks the previous evening. The Nasdaq fell 5.5% on Thursday (5 November), its biggest one-day decline in 18 months. This was largely driven by investor concerns that the US Democratic Party’s sweeping victory in the midterm elections could lead to tighter regulation of the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, particularly restrictions on data centre expansion. That, in turn, could dampen expectations for demand for advanced chips and related equipment.

The STAR 50 Index, which includes several leading Chinese AI and semiconductor stocks, closed 2.6% lower on Friday. Even before that, it had plunged nearly 30% over the previous three months. In other words, the AI-driven stock market boom had already begun to cool in China.

This AI boom can be traced back to early last year, when Chinese AI company DeepSeek burst onto the scene with its large language model, fuelling a technology stock rally. Global hedge funds poured into the Chinese market at an accelerating pace, adding more than US$1.3 trillion (S$1.67 trillion) to the combined market value of Chinese stocks traded onshore and offshore within a month.

AI quickly became one of the hottest investment themes in China’s capital markets. From large AI models and chips to data centres and humanoid robots, a host of related companies rode the AI boom and became investor favourites.

Ahead of Chinese New Year this year, technology giant ByteDance launched its AI video generation model Seedance 2.0, sparking another AI-led rally in A-shares. Several related stocks hit their daily upper trading limits for consecutive days. Around the same time, large AI model developers Z.AI (previously known as Zhipu AI) and MiniMax listed in Hong Kong to an enthusiastic reception, setting off a rush by AI companies to go public.

Gold Reclaims $4,100 as Central Banks Buy 321 Tons in a Quarter, Most Since Late 2024
sum: In early trading on Nov. 5, Chinese precious-metals stocks rallied across the board. Shengda Resources (000603.SZ) sealed the daily limit, while Xingye Yinxi (000426.SZ), Chifeng Gold (600988.SS), Sichuan Gold (001337.SZ), Xiaocheng Technology (300139.SZ) and Zhaojin Gold (000506.SZ) all followed higher. The direct trigger for the sector's mood was the sustained rebound in international gold prices: COMEX gold climbed back above $4,100 an ounce, gaining more than $200 in just a few sessions.

A day earlier, on Nov. 4, spot gold had already moved first, breaking through the $4,000 an ounce mark in the afternoon and rising more than 3% on the day. It came within striking distance of $4,050 an ounce intraday, a single-day gain of about $116. As recently as the start of November, gold had briefly fallen below $3,900 an ounce, touching an intraday low of $3,874.30 — a sharp V-shaped swing over just a few days that had the market calling it a roller-coaster.
Weaker dollar and Treasury yields act as the direct catalyst

In the view of Everbright Futures, the most direct trigger for this rebound was the simultaneous pullback in the dollar index and Treasury yields after the outcome of the U.S. midterm elections became clear. For gold, a softer dollar and falling yields occurring at the same time is a highly favorable combination.

A CITIC Securities research note offered a policy-path interpretation: with the Democratic Party winning control of Congress, the positive impact on gold prices could come through two channels. First, if war funding is cut, it could make the medium-term outlook for the U.S.-Iran situation clearer, helping to lower inflation expectations and in turn easing expectations of tightening. Second, if regulatory measures in some emerging sectors become stricter, it could help lower inflation expectations tied to large-scale capital spending in the short to medium term, while also potentially raising concerns about long-term growth momentum.

Swings in rate-hike expectations are equally key. According to CME's "FedWatch" data, the probability that the Federal Reserve leaves rates unchanged in December is 21.1%, while the probability of a 25-basis-point hike is 78.9%.

China Bond Market Selloff Hits Wealth Product NAVs; Major Bank Wealth Units Urge Investors to 'Hold Steady'
sum: From late October into early November, a sharp bond market slide triggered by a credit-risk event is being transmitted along the net asset value (NAV) curve to tens of thousands of holders of bank wealth management products. Over the two trading sessions of October 30 and November 2, the NAVs of multiple R2-level (low-to-medium risk) fixed-income products fell consecutively, with some posting single-day drawdowns of 6 basis points. Facing concentrated investor anxiety, several wealth management firms—including ICBC Wealth Management, ABC Wealth Management, Huaxia Wealth Management and Ningyin Wealth Management—issued statements in quick succession explaining the causes of the volatility and urging holders to avoid emotional redemptions.

The immediate trigger for this round of adjustment emerged last Friday. Pressured by escalating debt-repayment concerns at Huafa and a contraction in month-end liquidity, China's long-rallying bond market abruptly reversed, with yields on both rate bonds and credit bonds rising sharply in tandem. In the interbank market, the yield on the 30-year Chinese government bond "26 Ultra-Long Special Treasury Bond 04" rose intraday by more than 4 basis points to 2.096%, while the 10-year "26 Interest-Bearing Treasury Bond 16" climbed above 1.64%. Yields on actively traded 2-year, 3-year and 5-year notes rose 2.4, 2.5 and 2.5 basis points, respectively. That day, some wealth management funds preemptively redeemed bond funds—a move market participants viewed as a key factor amplifying the decline.

What weighed on NAVs even more was that the bond market adjustment coincided with a stock market slump. A-shares had been adjusting persistently since the second half of the year, already pressuring returns on "fixed income plus" products, and last Friday's continued equity market decline formed a rare "double kill" across stocks and bonds.

Standard Bank wins four global awards for digital banking innovation
sum: At The Digital Banker’s Global Retail Banking Innovation Awards 2026 in Singapore, Standard Bank won four top accolades, cementing its status as an industry leader in hyper-personalisation.

“Our clients remain at the centre of every solution we build. Smart Pulse, our real-time hyper-personalisation capability, enables us to sense, learn, decide and act in moments that matter, creating more relevant and timely experiences that deliver greater value for our clients,” says Funeka Montjane, CEO of personal and private banking at Standard Bank Group.

“Winning on the international stage demonstrates that solutions built around the needs of South African clients can stand alongside the best in the world, while delivering real impact where it matters most: in our clients’ everyday lives.”

The awards were presented at a gala at the Marina Bay Sands Convention Centre in Singapore on 22 October 2026. Standard Bank was recognised in four categories: Excellence in Digital Innovation – South Africa; Outstanding Innovation in Digital Banking – South Africa; Best Digital Banking Initiative – South Africa; and Best Marketing Personalisation Across Channels.

Now in their ninth year, the Global Retail Banking Innovation Awards recognise retail banks around the world. Entries are assessed by a judging panel that includes senior advisers from Accenture, Bain & Company, Deloitte, Kearney, KPMG and Simon-Kucher.

Among the initiatives recognised was Smart Pulse, Standard Bank’s real-time hyper-personalisation capability. Developed in response to growing client expectations for immediate, relevant and contextual banking experiences, Smart Pulse combines streaming data, machine learning, intelligent decisioning and an event-driven architecture to identify and respond to client needs in the moments that matter. So far this year, Smart Pulse has powered hundreds of millions of intelligent, service-triggered engagements across more than 35 service and sales use cases. These engagements are driving take-up of relevant products and services, while proactively connecting clients to the services and solutions they need most.

Death Cross Pressure, ICBC Stock Gains 1.48% on Friday
sum: On October 30, 2026: price 7.90 HKD, trend sideways, RSI 62.8, support 7.24, resistance 7.89. technical analysis of icbc stock. Death Cross Pressure — full…

ICBC closed at HK$7.90 on Friday, October 30, 2026, after turnover jumped to 1.5 times its 20-session average, according to the supplied exchange data. The advance put the stock near its three-month high and above the upper Bollinger Band, while a recent death cross points the other way. That mix makes the move worth watching: trading activity confirms participation, but momentum is pressing against nearby resistance as a bearish moving-average signal remains in place.

ICBC rose 1.48% in one day and 9.05% over five days, leaving it 2.40% higher over one month. The stock finished at the highest level of its 20-session range, with resistance at HK$7.89, and sat close to its three-month high of HK$7.91. The small gap between the close and that peak suggests buyers have driven price into a zone where further progress may require fresh demand.

The technical backdrop is less decisive than the price move. At HK$7.90, the stock was above its 20-day simple moving average (SMA) of HK$7.55, but that average was marginally below the 50-day SMA of HK$7.56. The resulting death cross—formed two sessions before the latest session—is a bearish signal because it indicates the shorter-term average has slipped beneath the longer-term one. It is not, by itself, proof that the latest rally has failed: the 20-day average’s slope was nearly flat, rising just 0.05% over five days.

As shown in the chart, price has moved above the upper Bollinger Band at HK$7.84. Bollinger Bands mark a range around a moving average; a close beyond the upper band can reflect strong buying, but it can also signal that price has stretched ahead of its recent norm. The band width was narrowing at 7.5%, a squeeze that can precede a larger move without indicating its direction.

Momentum measures are positive but not unanimous. The RSI was 62.8, a neutral reading: it reflects improving strength without reaching the commonly watched overbought threshold. MACD was also constructive, with the indicator at 0.034, above its -0.001 signal line, and a positive 0.035 histogram. In plain terms, the shorter-term momentum reading has turned upward.

SpaceX stock jumps after record IPO, making Musk the first trillionaire
sum: The company is expected to be included in the Nasdaq 100 within weeks

SpaceX soared in its Nasdaq debut on Friday, sending its value past $2 trillion US, as investors jumped at the chance to get a piece of Elon Musk's sprawling empire spanning rockets, internet service and AI after a record-setting IPO.

Trade kicked off late Friday morning, swinging for most of the session between gains of 15 per cent and 30 per cent above Thursday's pricing with little in the way of volatility. Shares ended the day at about $161 a share, up 19 per cent, making SpaceX the sixth-largest U.S. company, though the final settlement price had yet to be determined.

The trading, which surpassed 500 million shares, or about $80 billion US in volume, capped off a lead-up fraught with anxiety over the exchange's ability to handle the launch, particularly after a recent swoon in technology shares that raised concerns about the massive gains in AI-linked names.

With mega-listings from AI heavyweights Anthropic and OpenAI waiting in the wings, market watchers worried that a flood of new IPOs could hurt market performance following a long period with a relative dearth of offerings. But investors across the spectrum, from large institutions to retail fans of Musk, ended the day euphoric.

Here’s why the HSBC share price is in a strong bull run
sum: HSBC share price continued its strong rally and is now sitting at its all-time high, with its market capitalization hitting $300 billion. It has become the sixth biggest bank in the world after JPMorgan, Bank of America, ICBC, Agriculture Bank of China, and China Construction Bank. This article explores whether the stock has more upside to go.
HSBC, a top European bank, has been in a strong uptrend in the past few years, moving from a low of 277p in 2021 to the current 1,277p.
This surge has mirrored the performance of other European banks like Société Générale, UniCredit, Lloyds Bank, and Commerzbank.
